fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. Jesus says God "will also glorify the Son in Himself—and will glorify Him at once." At once is the opposite of a long wait. So the answer here is no.

Not this time, friend. John 13:22 says, "The disciples looked at one another, perplexed as to which of them He meant." They didn't know which of them He meant. I think that was a very quiet, awkward dinner table.

Yes, baker! Peter motioned to the disciple at Jesus' side to ask Jesus which one He was talking about. I think that's like a man trying to get a waiter's attention in a packed restaurant. Then the disciple leaned back and asked.
The text never mentions a door, friend. John 13:24 says Peter motioned to the disciple to ask Jesus which one He was talking about. That's a question, not a guard post.
Good guess, but the text doesn't say Jesus pointed. He gave the sign: "It is the one to whom I give this morsel after I have dipped it." Then He dipped it and gave it to Judas son of Simon Iscariot.

You got it, baker. John 13:28 says, "But no one at the table knew why Jesus had said this to him." Not one person at the table knew why. I think they were all just as lost as I am when somebody says "it's a quick fix" and hands me a wrench.

The text doesn't mention paying the owner of the house, friend. John 13:29 says some thought Jesus was telling Judas "…to buy what was needed for the feast, or to give something to the poor." Paying an owner isn't one of those guesses.

The text doesn't say anything about hiding the bag, friend. Some thought Jesus was telling Judas "…to buy what was needed for the feast, or to give something to the poor." Since Judas kept the money bag, the guesses it gives are about buying and giving, not hiding.
No, Judas didn't stay, friend. John 13:30 says, "As soon as he had received the morsel, Judas went out into the night." He went out. Going out into the night is the opposite of sitting back down.
The text doesn't say that, friend. Jesus says, "Where I am going, you cannot come." That's the whole line, and I think it doesn't sound like a stroll around the block.
These verses don't mention the prophets, friend. Jesus says, "As I have loved you, so you also must love one another." The example He holds up is His own love for them.
The text doesn't record Peter asking that, friend. John 13:36 says Simon Peter asked, "Lord, where are You going?" It's a question about where Jesus is going.
That's right, baker. Peter says, "Lord, why can't I follow You now?" He asks something more. I'd have asked a lot of questions too, probably with my mustache flapping.
That's not in the text, friend. What Peter promises is, "I will lay down my life for You." It's a promise about himself and nothing else. The words are about his own life.
